definition: The visual part of the website that users see and interact with (buttons, text, layout, forms).
The behind-the-scenes server that processes login requests, security checks, and data calculations.
A secure digital storage system where your website saves permanent data like user accounts and orders.
The messenger bridge that transfers data between your frontend website screens and backend server.
The folder on your computer (or GitHub) containing all your website's files, images, and code history.
A free version-control tool that saves snapshots of your work so you can safely undo mistakes.
The process of uploading your finished website code from your laptop to cloud servers so anyone on the internet can visit it.
A secret configuration file used to store private passwords, database keys, and API tokens safely.
Short for Create, Read, Update, Delete—the 4 basic operations performed on any database record.
A security checkpoint guard that checks if a user is logged in before letting them access protected pages.
